Name: Ledger Notebook
Tagline: A5 dot grid, 192 pages, lies flat from the first page.
Description: The notebook the studio uses for everything from press logs to grocery lists. Thread-sewn signatures open flat without cracking, and the 100 gsm paper takes fountain pen ink without feathering or bleed. Numbered pages and a two-page index at the front mean you can actually find things again.
Material: 100 gsm cream paper, cloth spine, board cover
Highlights: Thread-sewn binding opens flat|Numbered pages with index|Fountain-pen friendly 100 gsm paper|Two ribbon markers

Name: Pocket Journal, set of three
Tagline: Saddle-stitched, 48 pages each, fits a back pocket.
Description: Three slim journals with a kraft cover and a different ruling in each: lined, dot grid, and plain. Saddle-stitched with two staples so they stay flat and cheap enough to fill with nonsense. Round corners survive a month in a coat pocket.
Highlights: Three rulings: lined, dot, plain|Rounded corners|Fits a back pocket|Printed and stitched in the studio

Name: Weekly Planner
Tagline: Undated. One week per spread, a column for what actually happened.
Description: A planner with no dates printed in it, so a missed month costs nothing. Each spread holds a week on the left and a free page on the right for the things that were not planned. Starts whenever you start.
Highlights: Undated weeks|Free page opposite every week|Lies flat|Elastic closure and pen loop

Name: Landscape Sketchbook
Tagline: Wide format for maps, plans, and the long view.
Description: A sketchbook that is wider than it is tall, for drawings that run sideways. Heavy 160 gsm paper takes pencil, ink, and a light wash. Bound with exposed thread so it opens completely flat on the table.
Material: 160 gsm drawing paper, exposed coptic binding
Highlights: 160 gsm drawing paper|Opens fully flat|Landscape format|Takes light washes

Name: Brass Fountain Pen
Tagline: A pen with some weight to it, medium steel nib.
Description: Machined from solid brass and left unlacquered so it darkens with your hand. The steel nib is a wet medium that suits the studio's inks. Takes standard international cartridges or the included converter.
Highlights: Unlacquered brass develops a patina|Medium steel nib|Cartridge or converter|Machined, not cast

Name: Clutch Pencil, 2 mm
Tagline: The drafting pencil that lives on the press bench.
Description: A 2 mm lead holder with a knurled grip and a sharpener hidden in the push button. Holds a lead firmly enough to draw a serif and releases it with one click. Ships with two HB leads.
Highlights: 2 mm lead for long points|Sharpener in the cap|Knurled grip|Two HB leads included

Name: Harbour Blue Ink
Description: The ink we mix for the press, reformulated for fountain pens. A working blue with a little black in it, so it looks like the harbour on a weekday rather than a postcard. Shades nicely on good paper and behaves on bad.
Highlights: Mixed by weight, not by eye|Shades on good paper|Washable|Glass bottle with a wide mouth

Name: Studio Pencils, box of twelve
Description: Twelve plain cedar pencils with a dense HB core that holds a point. Left unpainted because paint hides the grain and because you will sharpen it off anyway. Stamped with the studio mark on one face.
Highlights: Twelve HB pencils|Unpainted cedar|Hexagonal barrel|Stamped, not printed

Name: Walnut Pen Tray
Tagline: Three channels, one shallow well, no more rolling off the desk.
Description: Carved from a single piece of black walnut and finished with oil. Three channels keep pens, pencils, and a ruler apart, and the shallow well at the end collects clips, erasers, and the small brass things that otherwise vanish.
Highlights: Single piece of walnut|Three pen channels|Oil finish, easily renewed|Cork feet

Name: Linen Desk Pad
Tagline: A quiet surface for writing, 60 by 40 centimetres.
Description: Heavy natural linen bonded to a cork backing. It gives a pen something to push against, keeps a desk from clattering, and rolls up when you need the whole table for something else.
Highlights: Natural linen face|Cork backing grips the desk|Rolls for storage|Wipe clean

Name: Brass Ruler, 30 cm
Tagline: Metric and imperial, and heavy enough to cut against.
Description: A straightedge with a bevelled edge for knife work and a flat edge for pencil. Markings are engraved rather than printed so they will outlast the hand that uses them. Solid brass, so it stays where you put it.
Highlights: Engraved markings|Bevelled cutting edge|Metric and imperial|Hanging hole

Name: Studio Task Lamp
Tagline: An articulated lamp with a warm, dimmable bulb.
Description: Two arms, three joints, and a weighted base that does not need a clamp. The shade throws a wide, warm pool that is kind to paper and eyes. Dims with a knob on the base rather than an app.
Highlights: Three articulated joints|Dimmer knob on the base|Warm 2700 K bulb included|Weighted base, no clamp

Name: Canvas Tool Roll
Tagline: Eight pockets and a strap, for pens, knives, and brushes.
Description: Waxed canvas with eight graduated pockets and a flap that keeps everything from sliding out. Rolls tight and ties with a leather strap. Holds a dozen pencils, a knife, a ruler, and a pair of scissors with room to spare.
Highlights: Eight graduated pockets|Waxed canvas sheds water|Leather tie strap|Flap keeps tools in

Name: Leather Pen Sleeve
Tagline: Holds two pens. Gets better with age.
Description: A simple sleeve cut from vegetable-tanned leather and saddle-stitched by hand. Fits two full-size pens or three pencils. Starts stiff and pale and ends up soft and dark, which is the point.
